title: Optical illusions show how we see
speaker: Beau Lotto

sentences.en: Before I get started: I'm really excited to be here to just actually watch what's going to happen, from here.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前：我很高兴能够在这里亲眼目睹将要发生的事情。

sentences.en: So with that said, we're going to start with: What is one of our greatest needs, one of our greatest needs for our brain?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我们要从以下问题开始：我们最大的需求之一、我们大脑的最大需求之一是什么？

sentences.en: And instead of telling you, I want to show you.
sentences.zh: 我不想告诉你，而是想向你展示。

sentences.en: In fact, I want you to feel it. There's a lot I want you to feel in the next 14 minutes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想让你感受一下。我希望你在接下来的 14 分钟内感受到很多东西。

sentences.en: So, if we could all stand up. We're all going to conduct a piece of Strauss together.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们都能站起来。我们要一起指挥一首施特劳斯的作品。

sentences.en: Alright? And you all know it. Alright. Are you ready?
sentences.zh: 好吧？你们都知道。好吧。你准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Audience: Yeah! Beau Lotto: Alright. Ready, one, two, three!
sentences.zh: 观众：是啊！博洛托：好的。准备好，一、二、三！

sentences.en: It's just the end. (Music: Richard Strauss "Also Sprach Zarathustra") Right?
sentences.zh: 这只是结束。 （音乐：理查·施特劳斯《查拉图斯特拉如是说》）对吧？

sentences.en: You know where it's going. (Music) Oh, it's coming!
sentences.zh: 你知道它要去哪里。 （音乐）哦，来了！

sentences.en: (Music stops abruptly) Oh! (Laughter) Right?
sentences.zh: （音乐突然停止）哦！ （笑声）对吧？

sentences.en: Collective coitus interruptus. OK, you can all sit down.
sentences.zh: 集体性交中断。好啦，大家可以坐下了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) We have a fundamental need for closure.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我们有一个基本的需要：结束。

sentences.en: (Laughter) We love closure. (Applause) I was told the story that Mozart, just before he'd go to bed, he'd go to the piano and go, "da-da-da-da-da."
sentences.zh: （笑声）我们喜欢结束。 （掌声）我听说莫扎特在睡觉前会走到钢琴前，唱出“哒哒哒哒哒哒”的故事。

sentences.en: His father, who was already in bed, would think, "Argh."
sentences.zh: 他的父亲已经躺在床上了，他会想：“啊。”

sentences.en: He'd have to get up and hit the final note to the chord before he could go back to sleep.
sentences.zh: 他必须站起来，敲出和弦的最后一个音符，然后才能回去睡觉。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So the need for closure leads us to thinking about: What is our greatest fear?
sentences.zh: （笑声）所以结束的需要让我们思考：我们最大的恐惧是什么？

sentences.en: Think -- what is our greatest fear growing up, even now?
sentences.zh: 想一想——即使是现在，我们成长过程中最大的恐惧是什么？

sentences.en: And it's the fear of the dark. We hate uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这就是对黑暗的恐惧。我们讨厌不确定性。

sentences.en: We hate to not know. We hate it. Think about horror films.
sentences.zh: 我们讨厌不知道。我们讨厌它。想想恐怖片。

sentences.en: Horror films are always shot in the dark, in the forest, at night, in the depths of the sea, the blackness of space.
sentences.zh: 恐怖片总是在黑暗中拍摄，在森林里，在夜晚，在大海深处，在漆黑的太空中。

sentences.en: And the reason is because dying was easy during evolution.
sentences.zh: 原因是因为在进化过程中死亡是很容易的。

sentences.en: If you weren't sure that was a predator, it was too late.
sentences.zh: 如果你不确定那是掠食者，那就太晚了。

sentences.en: Your brain evolved to predict. And if you couldn't predict, you died.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑进化出了预测能力。如果你无法预测，你就死了。

sentences.en: And the way your brain predicts is by encoding the bias and assumptions that were useful in the past.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑预测的方式是对过去有用的偏见和假设进行编码。

sentences.en: But those assumptions just don't stay inside your brain.
sentences.zh: 但这些假设不会留在你的大脑中。

sentences.en: You project them out into the world. There is no bird there.
sentences.zh: 你把它们投射到世界里 那里没有鸟

sentences.en: You're projecting the meaning onto the screen.
sentences.zh: 你把意义投射到屏幕上

sentences.en: Everything I'm saying to you right now is literally meaningless.
sentences.zh: 我现在对你说的一切都毫无意义

sentences.en: (Laughter) You're creating the meaning and projecting it onto me.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 你创造了意义 并把它投射到我身上。

sentences.en: And what's true for objects is true for other people.
sentences.zh: 物体是真实的 其他人也是一样

sentences.en: While you can measure their "what" and their "when," you can never measure their "why."
sentences.zh: 当你能测量他们的"什么"和"什么时候" 你永远无法测量他们的"为什么"

sentences.en: So we color other people. We project a meaning onto them based on our biases and our experience.
sentences.zh: 所以,我们给其他人颜色。我们根据我们的偏见和我们的经验,向他们展示了一种意义。

sentences.en: Which is why the best of design is almost always about decreasing uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么最好的设计 几乎总是关于减少不确定性。

sentences.en: So when we step into uncertainty, our bodies respond physiologically and mentally.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们进入不确定状态时, 我们的身体在生理和精神上的反应。

sentences.en: Your immune system will start deteriorating.
sentences.zh: 你的免疫系统会开始恶化

sentences.en: Your brain cells wither and even die. Your creativity and intelligence decrease.
sentences.zh: 你的脑细胞枯萎甚至死亡 你的创造力和智力都下降了

sentences.en: We often go from fear to anger, almost too often.
sentences.zh: 我们经常从恐惧变成愤怒,几乎太频繁了。

sentences.en: Why? Because fear is a state of certainty.
sentences.zh: 为什么 因为恐惧是肯定的

sentences.en: You become morally judgmental. You become an extreme version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 你变成道德上的判断,你变成你自己的极端版本

sentences.en: If you're a conservative, you become more conservative.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个保守派 你就会变得更保守

sentences.en: If you're a liberal, you become more liberal.
sentences.zh: 如果你是自由派,你就会变得更加自由。

sentences.en: Because you go to a place of familiarity.
sentences.zh: 因为你去一个熟悉的地方

sentences.en: The problem is that the world changes. And we have to adapt or die.
sentences.zh: 问题在于世界会改变,我们必须适应,否则会死。

sentences.en: And if you want to shift from A to B, the first step is not B.
sentences.zh: 如果你想从A到B 第一步不是B

sentences.en: The first step is to go from A to not A -- to let go of your bias and assumptions; to step into the very place that our brain evolved to avoid; to step into the place of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 第一步是从A到非A-- 放弃你的偏见和假设; 进入我们大脑的进化地 来避免; 进入未知的地方。

sentences.en: But it's so essential that we go to this place that our brain gave us a solution.
sentences.zh: 但它是如此重要,我们去这个地方 我们的大脑给了我们一个解决方案。

sentences.en: Evolution gave us a solution. And it's possibly one of the most profound perceptual experiences.
sentences.zh: 进化给了我们一个解决方案。它可能是 最深刻的感官体验之一。

sentences.en: And it's the experience of awe. (Music) (Applause)
sentences.zh: 这是敬畏的体验

sentences.en: (Music) (Applause) (Music)
sentences.zh: (掌声) (掌声)

sentences.en: (Applause) (Music) (Applause)
sentences.zh: (掌声) (音乐) (掌声)

sentences.en: (Cheers) (Applause) Beau Lotto: Ah, how wonderful, right?
sentences.zh: (掌声) Beau Lotto: 啊,多棒啊,对吗?

sentences.en: So right now, you're probably all feeling, at some level or another, awe.
sentences.zh: 所以,现在,你们可能都感觉, 在某些级别或其它级别, 敬畏。

sentences.en: Right? So what's happening inside your brain right now?
sentences.zh: 你脑子里现在发生了什么?

sentences.en: And for thousands of years, we've been thinking and writing and experiencing awe, and we know so little about it.
sentences.zh: 几千年来 我们一直在思考 写作 体验敬畏 我们对此知之甚少

sentences.en: And so to try to understand what is it and what does it do, my Lab of Misfits had just the wonderful opportunity and the pleasure to work with who are some of the greatest creators of awe that we know:
sentences.zh: 所以为了理解它是什么 和它做什么, 我的错误实验室 刚刚得到了一个美妙的机会 和快乐的工作 与谁是 一些最伟大的创造者 敬畏,我们知道:

sentences.en: the writers, the creators, the directors, the accountants, the people who are Cirque Du Soleil.
sentences.zh: 作家,创作者, 董事,会计, 人民谁是Cirque Du Soleil。

sentences.en: And so we went to Las Vegas, and we recorded the brain activity of people while they're watching the performance, over 10 performances of "O," which is iconic Cirque performance.
sentences.zh: 于是我们去了拉斯维加斯, 我们记录了人们的大脑活动, 当他们正在看表演时, 超过10场“O”表演, 这是标志性的圆形表演。

sentences.en: And we also measured the behavior before the performance, as well as a different group after the performance.
sentences.zh: 我们还测量了表演前的行为 以及表演后的不同群体

sentences.en: And so we had over 200 people involved. So what is awe?
sentences.zh: 所以,我们有200多人参与其中。那什么是敬畏?

sentences.en: What is happening inside your brain right now?
sentences.zh: 你脑子里到底发生了什么?

sentences.en: It's a brain state. OK? The front part of your brain, the prefrontal cortex, which is responsible for your executive function, your attentional control, is now being downregulated.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大脑状态。好吗?你的大脑的前部部分, 前额皮层, 负责您的行政功能, 你的注意力控制, 现在正在下降管制。

sentences.en: The part of your brain called the DMN, default mode network, which is the interaction between multiple areas in your brain, which is active during, sort of, ideation, creative thinking in terms of divergent thinking and daydreaming,
sentences.zh: 你大脑的一部分叫做DMN 默认模式网络, 也就是你大脑中多个区域之间的相互作用, 在不同的思维和白日梦中活跃, 思想,创造性思维,

sentences.en: is now being upregulated. And right about now, the activity in your prefrontal cortex is changing.
sentences.zh: 现在,你的前额皮层活动正在发生变化。

sentences.en: It's becoming asymmetrical in its activity, biased towards the right, which is highly correlated when people step forward into the world, as opposed to step back.
sentences.zh: 它的活动变得不对称,偏向于权利, 当人们踏入世界,而不是退步时, 权利就高度相关。

sentences.en: In fact, the activity across the brains of all these people was so correlated that we're able to train an artificial neural network to predict whether or not people are experiencing awe to an accuracy of 75 percent on average,
sentences.zh: 事实上,所有这些人的大脑之间的活动非常相关 以至于我们可以训练一个人工神经网络 来预测人们是否 正在经历恐惧

sentences.en: with a maximum of 83 percent. So what does this brain state do?
sentences.zh: 最多为83%。这个大脑状态会做什么?

sentences.en: Well, others have demonstrated, for instance, Professors Haidt and Keltner, have told us that people feel small but connected to the world.
sentences.zh: 其他人也证明了,例如,海特教授和凯尔特纳教授告诉我们,人们感到自己很小,但与世界有联系。

sentences.en: And their prosocial behavior increases, because they feel an increased affinity towards others.
sentences.zh: 他们的亲社会行为会增加, 因为他们对他人的亲情会增加。

sentences.en: And we've also shown in this study that people have less need for cognitive control.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究还显示 人们对认知控制的需求较少。

sentences.en: They're more comfortable with uncertainty without having closure.
sentences.zh: 他们更适应不确定因素 而不关闭。

sentences.en: And their appetite for risk also increases.
sentences.zh: 他们对风险的胃口也增加了

sentences.en: They actually seek risk, and they are better able at taking it.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上寻求风险,他们更有能力承担风险。

sentences.en: And something that was really quite profound is that when we asked people, "Are you someone who has a propensity to experience awe?"
sentences.zh: 真正深刻的是 当我们问人们, “你是一个有恐惧倾向的人吗?”

sentences.en: They were more likely to give a positive response after the performance than they were [before].
sentences.zh: 与[以前]相比,他们更有可能在表演后做出积极回应。

sentences.en: They literally redefined themselves and their history.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上重新定义了自己和他们的历史。

sentences.en: So, awe is possibly the perception that is bigger than us.
sentences.zh: 因此,敬畏可能是比我们更大的感觉。

sentences.en: And in the words of Joseph Campbell, "Awe is what enables us to move forward."
sentences.zh: 用约瑟夫·坎贝尔的话来说,“我们是能使我们前进的。”

sentences.en: Or in the words of a dear friend, probably one of our greatest photographers, still living photographers, Duane Michaels, he said to me just the other day that maybe it gives us the curiosity to overcome our cowardice.
sentences.zh: 或者用一个亲爱的朋友的话来说, 也许是我们最伟大的摄影师之一, 仍然活着的摄影师,Duane Michaels, 他几天前对我说, 也许这给了我们一种好奇心来克服我们的懦弱。

sentences.en: So who cares? Why should we care? Well, consider conflict, which seems to be so omnipresent in our society at the moment.
sentences.zh: 那么,谁在乎呢?我们为什么要在乎呢?那么,考虑一下冲突,现在在我们社会上似乎无处不在。

sentences.en: If you and I are in conflict, it's as if we're at the opposite ends of the same line.
sentences.zh: 如果你和我有冲突 我们就好像在同一条线的对面

sentences.en: And my aim is to prove that you're wrong and to shift you towards me.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是证明你错了 把你转嫁给我

sentences.en: The problem is, you are doing exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 问题是,你做的完全一样。

sentences.en: You're trying to prove that I'm wrong and shift me towards you.
sentences.zh: 你是想证明我错了 把我推到你身上

sentences.en: Notice that conflict is the setup to win but not learn.
sentences.zh: 注意冲突是赢得而非学习的场景。

sentences.en: Your brain only learns if we move. Life is movement.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑只有在我们移动时才会学习 生活就是运动

sentences.en: So, what if we could use awe, not to get rid of conflict -- conflict is essential, conflict is how your brain expands, it's how your brain learns -- but rather, to enter conflict in a different way?
sentences.zh: 那么,如果我们能利用敬畏,而不是摆脱冲突-- 冲突是不可或缺的, 冲突是你的大脑是如何膨胀的, 是你的大脑是如何学习的-- 而是以不同的方式进入冲突?

sentences.en: And what if awe could enable us to enter it in at least two different ways?
sentences.zh: 如果敬畏能让我们 以至少两种不同的方式进入它呢?

sentences.en: One, to give us the humility and courage to not know.
sentences.zh: 第一,给予我们谦卑 和勇气不知道。

sentences.en: Right? To enter conflict with a question instead of an answer.
sentences.zh: 与一个问题而不是一个答案发生冲突。

sentences.en: What would happen then? To enter the conflict with uncertainty instead of certainty.
sentences.zh: 然后会发生什么? 以不确定性而不是确定性进入冲突。

sentences.en: And the second is, in entering conflict that way, to seek to understand, rather than convince.
sentences.zh: 第二个是,在以这种方式进入冲突时,寻求理解而不是说服。

sentences.en: Because everyone makes sense to themselves, right?
sentences.zh: 因为每个人都对自己有意义,对吗?

sentences.en: And to understand another person, is to understand the biases and assumptions that give rise to their behavior.
sentences.zh: 要理解另一个人 就是要理解导致他们行为的偏见和假设

sentences.en: And we've actually initiated a pilot study to look to see whether we could use art-induced awe to facilitate toleration.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上已经启动了一个试点研究 看看我们是否可以使用 艺术诱发的敬畏来帮助容忍。

sentences.en: And the results are actually incredibly positive.
sentences.zh: 结果实在是令人难以置信的乐观。

sentences.en: We can mitigate against anger and hate through the experience of awe generated by art.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过艺术创造的敬畏感来减轻愤怒和仇恨。

sentences.en: So where can we find awe, given how important it is?
sentences.zh: 因此,我们在哪里可以找到敬畏, 鉴于它是多么重要?

sentences.en: So, what if ... A suggestion: that awe is not just to be found in the grandeur.
sentences.zh: 那么,如果... 一个建议: 敬畏不只是在光荣中找到。

sentences.en: Awe is essential. Often, it's scale -- the mountains, the sunscape.
sentences.zh: 敬畏是必需的。通常,它是规模的-- 山,日出。

sentences.en: But what if we could actually rescale ourselves and find the impossible in the simple?
sentences.zh: 但如果我们真的可以 调整自己的规模 并发现不可能 在简单?

sentences.en: And if this is true, and our data are right, then endeavors like science, adventure, art, ideas, love,
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的,我们的数据是正确的, 那么努力,比如科学,冒险,艺术,思想,爱,

sentences.en: a TED conference, performance, are not only inspired by awe, but could actually be our ladders into uncertainty to help us expand.
sentences.zh: 一个TED会议,表演, 不仅受到敬畏的启发, 而且实际上可以成为我们 进入不确定性的阶梯 来帮助我们扩张。

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause) Please, come up.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢 请上来吧

sentences.en: (Applause) (Cheers) (Applause)
sentences.zh: (掌声)(掌声)(掌声)
